election.name: Illinois General Primary Election
election.earlyVoting: Lincoln Park Branch Library, 1150 W. Fullerton Ave.
election.note: Voters must declare a party (Democratic, Republican, or Libertarian) to receive a partisan ballot. Choosing Independent gives you only referenda. The Democratic primary winner is heavily favored in every race listed here — this district is D+19 or stronger at every level.

races.title: U.S. Senate — Illinois
races.description: Dick Durbin is retiring after holding this seat since 1997 — the first open Senate seat in Illinois since 2010. The winner of the March 17 primary faces the opposing party's nominee on November 3, 2026.

candidates.name: Raja Krishnamoorthi
candidates.bio: U.S. Representative for IL-8 (northwest suburbs near O'Hare) since 2017. Princeton mechanical engineering & public policy graduate; Harvard Law J.D. Former attorney, small-business owner, and deputy Illinois State Treasurer. An outspoken opponent of the Trump administration.
endorsements: Former Obama chief of staff Bill Daley

candidates.name: Robin Kelly
candidates.bio: U.S. Representative for IL-2 (south suburban) since 2013. Former Illinois state representative, chief of staff to State Treasurer Alexi Giannoulias, and chief administrative officer under Cook County Board President Toni Preckwinkle.

candidates.name: Juliana Stratton
candidates.bio: Illinois Lieutenant Governor since 2019, formerly an Illinois state representative. First to announce after Durbin's retirement and immediately endorsed by Governor Pritzker. Pritzker funneled $5 million into a super PAC supporting her.
priorities: Middle-class tax cuts funded by millionaire tax

candidates.name: Steve Botsford Jr.
candidates.bio: Northwest suburbs native. Notre Dame graduate who walked on to the football team. Worked on Capitol Hill for Rep. Tony Cárdenas drafting economic mobility legislation. Holds a master's in applied economics from Georgetown and an MBA from Northwestern.

candidates.name: Awisi A. Bustos
candidates.bio: Nonprofit executive and first-generation Ghanaian American. Former CEO of the Illinois Alliance of Boys & Girls Clubs, overseeing an $11 million budget.

candidates.name: Jonathan Dean
candidates.bio: Activist, entrepreneur, and litigator who describes himself as a proud survivor of childhood sexual abuse. Running to fight for young people, working families, and civil liberties.

candidates.name: Bryan Maxwell
candidates.bio: Assistant research scientist and project engineer at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign. Has organized to stop U.S. military aid to Israel.

candidates.name: Sean Brown
candidates.bio: Running in the Democratic primary for U.S. Senate.

candidates.name: Kevin Ryan
candidates.bio: Running in the Democratic primary for U.S. Senate.

candidates.name: Christopher Swann
candidates.bio: Running in the Democratic primary for U.S. Senate.

candidates.name: Don Tracy
candidates.bio: Attorney, former Illinois Republican Party chairman, and former Illinois Gaming Board chairman. Argues that with Durbin's retirement all statewide elected officials will be from Chicago or Cook County — leaving 101 downstate counties without a voice.

candidates.name: R. Cary Capparelli
candidates.bio: International businessman and educator. Son of longtime moderate Democratic state rep Ralph C. Capparelli. Career spanned the globe, including organizing the first U.S.–Soviet Union motorsports competitions.

candidates.name: Pamela Denise Long
candidates.bio: Occupational therapist and political commentator.

candidates.name: Casey Chlebek
candidates.bio: Polish immigrant, U.S. resident since the 1960s, longtime IT professional.
priorities: AI, robotics, and quantum computing investment

candidates.name: Jeannie Evans
candidates.bio: Running in the Republican primary for U.S. Senate.

candidates.name: Jimmy Lee Tillman II
candidates.bio: Running in the Republican primary for U.S. Senate.

candidates.name: Max Rice
candidates.bio: Running in the Republican primary for U.S. Senate.

candidates.name: Austin Mink
candidates.bio: Running as an independent candidate for U.S. Senate.

candidates.name: Tyrone Muhammad
candidates.bio: Running as an independent candidate for U.S. Senate.

candidates.name: Anthony Smith
candidates.bio: Running as an independent candidate for U.S. Senate.

races.title: U.S. House — Illinois 5th Congressional District
races.description: Ward 43 falls within IL-5, which covers the Far North Side (Lincoln Park, Lake View), northwest Chicago neighborhoods (Jefferson Park, Norwood Park), and northwest suburbs (Arlington Heights, Palatine). Cook PVI is D+19 — the primary is effectively the election. Incumbent Mike Quigley faces three Democratic challengers.

candidates.name: Mike Quigley
candidates.bio: Has represented IL-5 since 2009, age 67. Previously Cook County Commissioner. The Chicago Tribune editorial board calls him 'a genial and effective congressman, both principled and pragmatic.' Has reportedly soft-launched a potential run for Chicago mayor if he wins re-election.

candidates.name: Matthew Conroy
candidates.bio: 37-year-old former financial advisor and learning-development professional from Chicago. Highlights housing and child care costs as the defining affordability crises facing families in the district.

candidates.name: Ellen Corley
candidates.bio: Researcher from the Near North Side. Focuses on government accountability and systemic reform of institutions that have failed ordinary people.

candidates.name: Anthony Michael Tamez
candidates.bio: 26-year-old Native American candidate born and raised in IL-5. Elected to the Chicago Police District Council for the 17th District. Has worked with progressive aldermen on initiatives supporting Native and Black communities, youth programs, and public safety. Running to bring generational change to Congress.

candidates.name: Tom Hanson
candidates.bio: Running in the Republican primary for Illinois' 5th Congressional District.

candidates.name: Kimball Ladien
candidates.bio: Running in the Republican primary for Illinois' 5th Congressional District.

candidates.name: Barry Wicker
candidates.bio: Running in the Republican primary for Illinois' 5th Congressional District.

races.title: Governor / Lieutenant Governor
races.description: Governor and Lieutenant Governor run as a joint ticket in Illinois primaries and the general election. A third Pritzker term would be the first by a Democratic governor in Illinois history.

candidates.name: J.B. Pritzker / Christian Mitchell
candidates.bio: JB Pritzker has served as Governor since 2019. A billionaire heir to the Hyatt hotel fortune, he won in 2018 and 2022 by wide margins. Running mate Christian Mitchell served as deputy governor (2019–2023) and state representative (2013–2019). Pritzker is rumored to be eyeing a 2028 presidential run.

candidates.name: Darren Bailey / Aaron Del Mar
candidates.bio: Darren Bailey is a downstate farmer and former state senator who lost to Pritzker in the 2022 general election by about 11 points. Running mate Aaron Del Mar is a Cook County Republican aimed at broadening the ticket's suburban appeal.

candidates.name: James Mendrick / Running Mate TBD
candidates.bio: DuPage County Sheriff since 2018. Campaigning on public safety and has partnered with the DuPage County Health Department to provide Medication-Assisted Treatment to inmates fighting opioid addiction.

candidates.name: Ted Dabrowski / Carrie Mendoza
candidates.bio: Ted Dabrowski is president of a conservative news and policy website. Running mate Carrie Mendoza leads FAIR In Medicine.

candidates.name: Rick Heidner / Running Mate TBD
candidates.bio: Running in the Republican primary for Governor of Illinois.

races.title: Illinois State Senate — District 6
races.description: District 6 covers the lakefront Chicago neighborhoods of Lake View, Lincoln Park, and the Near North Side — Ward 43 is squarely in this district. Incumbent Sara Feigenholtz faces a progressive primary challenger for the first time in her 31-year career. The Chicago Tribune endorsed challenger Nick Uniejewski.

candidates.name: Sara Feigenholtz
candidates.bio: State Senator since 2020; before that, state representative of the 12th District from 1994. Age 69. Career focused on healthcare, social services, and LGBTQ+ rights. Backed by labor (Illinois Federation of Teachers, Teamsters) and establishment Democrats including Secretary of State Alexi Giannoulias.
candidates.note: The Illinois Democratic Party spent $190,000 on mailers supporting Feigenholtz — the most it has spent on any General Assembly candidate since September 2025.

candidates.name: Nick Uniejewski
candidates.bio: Policy analyst, formerly for the City of Chicago. Loyola University Chicago graduate (2017) with a DePaul graduate degree (2019). Would be the second openly gay state senator in Illinois history. Endorsed by North Side Ald. Leni Manaa-Hoppenworth (48th Ward) and former U.S. Rep. Marie Newman, for whom he served as campaign manager.
priorities: Housing supply (legalizing coach houses, zoning reform)

races.title: Illinois State House — District 12
races.description: District 12 covers the northern lakefront neighborhoods of Gold Coast, Old Town, Lincoln Park, and East Lakeview — Ward 43 is in this district. Incumbent Margaret Croke is leaving to run for state comptroller, making this an open seat. Four Democrats are competing in a relatively well-funded primary.

candidates.name: Paul Kendrick
candidates.bio: Former Barack Obama campaign and administration official. Has held leadership roles at nonprofits and the local Indivisible Chicago chapter. Endorsed by incumbent Rep. Margaret Croke and State Sen. Sara Feigenholtz. One of four legislative candidates statewide benefiting from a PAC funded by Meta (Facebook/Instagram parent).

candidates.name: Karim Lakhani
candidates.bio: Chief development officer for his family's Chicago-area hotel business. Campaign largely self-funded with family money. Endorsed by the Chicago Teachers Union (CTU).

candidates.name: Mac LeBuhn
candidates.bio: Former legal counsel and policy advisor to Mayor Lori Lightfoot. Emphasizes ethics reform and experience in city government. Endorsed by former Mayor Lightfoot, Chicago Growth Project, and several good-government aldermen.

candidates.name: Litcy Kurisinkal
candidates.bio: Biden 2020 campaign alumna. Attended protests of ICE operations at the Broadview detention facility in February 2026. Running the most grassroots campaign in the field.

candidates.name: Justin Kumar
candidates.bio: Running in the Republican primary for Illinois House District 12.

races.title: Illinois Comptroller
races.description: The Comptroller manages the state's finances, signs off on state payments, and provides financial oversight. Incumbent Susana Mendoza is not seeking re-election. Note: Democratic candidate Margaret Croke is currently the IL-12 state representative (the same seat being contested above).

candidates.name: Margaret Croke
candidates.bio: Illinois State Representative for District 12 (Lincoln Park, Old Town, Gold Coast) since 2021 — the same seat now being contested in the primary above. Running for comptroller rather than seeking re-election to the House.

candidates.name: Stephanie Kifowit
candidates.bio: State Representative for Aurora-area District 84 since 2013. Marine Corps veteran. Known for her advocacy on healthcare and veterans' issues.

candidates.name: Holly Kim
candidates.bio: Lake County Treasurer and Collector since 2018. First Korean American elected to countywide office in Illinois history.

candidates.name: Karina Villa
candidates.bio: Illinois State Senator for the 25th District (west suburbs) since 2019. Known for environmental and education legislation.

candidates.name: Bryan Drew
candidates.bio: Running as the Republican candidate for Illinois Comptroller.

races.title: Illinois Treasurer
races.description: The Treasurer manages and invests state funds and oversees college savings (Bright Start/Bright Directions) and financial literacy programs.

candidates.name: Mike Frerichs
candidates.bio: Illinois Treasurer since 2015. Former Champaign County state senator. Has expanded the Bright Start college savings program, returned record amounts of unclaimed property to residents, and launched financial inclusion initiatives.

candidates.name: Max Rice
candidates.bio: Running in the Republican primary for Illinois Treasurer.

candidates.name: Max Solomon
candidates.bio: Running in the Republican primary for Illinois Treasurer.

races.title: Cook County Board President
races.description: The Board President is the chief executive of Cook County, overseeing the county jail, court system, public health system (including Stroger Hospital), forest preserves, and a budget covering 20,000+ employees. This is a close, competitive race.

candidates.name: Toni Preckwinkle
candidates.bio: First Black woman elected Cook County Board President. Before that, 4th Ward alderman for nearly 20 years and a high school history teacher for 10 years. Has overseen four bond rating upgrades, forgiven $600M in medical debt for 500K+ residents, implemented major criminal justice reforms, and provided guaranteed income to 3,000+ households. March 17 is her 79th birthday.

candidates.name: Brendan Reilly
candidates.bio: 42nd Ward alderman since 2007, representing downtown Chicago (Loop, River North, Streeterville, Magnificent Mile). Age 54. Former Illinois House staffer and AT&T executive. Close ally of Mayor Rahm Emanuel, later critic of Mayor Lightfoot, and frequent critic of Mayor Brandon Johnson. Self-described independent and pro-business voice.
candidates.note: Preckwinkle has tied Reilly to Trump; Reilly says the Trump campaign donations he received were donated to charity.

races.title: Cook County Assessor
races.description: The Assessor sets the taxable value of all 1.8 million parcels in Cook County, directly determining property tax bills. This race pits a reform incumbent against a challenger with the Cook County Democratic Party organization's backing.

candidates.name: Fritz Kaegi
candidates.bio: Cook County Assessor since 2018. Former financial analyst who ran on a reform platform of eliminating historic disparities that over-assessed lower-value residential properties while under-assessing commercial properties. Has clashed with the Cook County Democratic organization throughout his tenure.
candidates.note: The Cook County Democratic Party endorsed his challenger, Pat Hynes, rather than the incumbent.

candidates.name: Pat Hynes
candidates.bio: Lyons Township Assessor and firefighter/EMT with the Western Springs Fire Department. Spent 23 years in the Cook County Assessor's office as a residential field inspector (including three under Kaegi). Nephew of former five-term Cook County Assessor and Illinois Senate President Thomas Hynes.
priorities: Using building permit data to improve accuracy
candidates.note: Has taken nearly $70,000 from property tax attorneys. Real estate industry donors favor Hynes over Kaegi.
